label: IMMENSE_1: a primitive predicate for being contained by no place and present to everything
definition: PRIMITIVE. Immense g: g is measured or contained by no place and is present to everything that is. After ST I q.8 (God is in all things as an agent is present to what it acts on, and in every place by giving it being). Counterexample: a body, which is contained by its place and absent from other places.
note: Explicitly identified primitive (Encode first). Open semantic obligation: typed accounts of place and of an agent's presence to its effect. Distinct from INFINITE_2 (quantitative or spatial infinity of extent): immensity here is not having infinite extent. Two open bridges constrain it, each giving a sufficient condition: 'Whatever causes the being of everything else is IMMENSE_1' and the weaker sense bridge 'Whatever is IMMENSE_2 is IMMENSE_1', from the typed sibling IMMENSE_2 (641c767b: infinite and causes the being of everything else; disambiguation 3fc3ee02). IMMENSE_2 types the grounds, not place, measure or presence by power and knowledge, so the typed account of place and presence remains open.
